source_name: data.gov.sk / open.slovensko.sk – Vestník VO open data (XML)
why_relevant: ÚVO publishes the procurement bulletin daily as XML on the national open-data portal (cooperation with NASES). This is the machine-readable backbone for a repeatable collector rather than scraping HTML.

source_name: Elektronická platforma / IS EPVO (elektronickaplatforma.sk)
why_relevant: The state's central electronic procurement platform (successor/companion to IS EVO) where tender documentation — technical specifications listing terminal counts, ATM models, service SLAs, cash volumes — is actually hosted and downloadable.

source_name: JOSEPHINE (PROEBIZ) – electronic tendering system
why_relevant: Second-most-used SK e-procurement system (~22% share). Many banks-adjacent and municipal buyers publish full tender documentation here; the public tender list is browsable without login and links to specification documents.

source_name: ERANET – procurement management system (incl. posta.eranet.sk)
why_relevant: Hosts tenders for major cash-relevant buyers; Slovenská pošta publishes its contracts announced since 1 Aug 2021 on its ERANET instance. Postal/branch cash-handling, cash transport and Poštomat ATM-related procurements surface here.

source_name: eZakazky – electronic public procurement platform
why_relevant: ~8% of SK electronic procurement runs through eZakazky; publishes tenders and enables supplier communication. Complements Josephine/ERANET for full coverage of where documentation lives.

source_name: Elektronický kontraktačný systém (EKS) / elektronické trhovisko
source_subtype: state electronic marketplace / dynamic purchasing system
why_relevant: Central state marketplace for commonly available goods and services, with ~100k concluded contracts. Low-value but high-frequency purchases — POS terminal accessories, cash registers, paper rolls, coin counters, ATM consumables — are visible here with unit prices and quantities, giving granular volume signals absent from big tenders.

source_name: UVOstat.sk – third-party analytics over ÚVO data (with API)
why_relevant: Restructures ÚVO bulletin and contract-register data into per-authority and per-supplier profiles with aggregate values, making it far faster to answer 'who buys/sells ATM and payment services to the SK state and for how much'. Documented API exists (token required).

source_name: TenderRadar.sk – multi-source SK/EU tender aggregator
why_relevant: Aggregates ÚVO, EKS, CRZ, Vestník VO and TED into one searchable stream — a convenient cross-check that a payments/ATM tender was not missed in any single register, and a pointer to which registers matter.

source_name: Tender.sk – commercial SK tender database and analytics
why_relevant: Operating since 2004 with branch-level classification; useful for categorised historical retrieval (e.g. logistics/cash services, IT/payment systems) and for spotting private-sector as well as state tenders.

source_name: Národná banka Slovenska – verejné obstarávanie / zmluvy, objednávky, faktúry
why_relevant: The central bank's own contract, order and invoice disclosures. Highly targeted for cash-cycle intelligence: banknote processing machines, cash sorting/authentication equipment, cash logistics, coin handling — exactly the equipment side of cash usage that no statistical release itemises.

source_name: Slovenská pošta – verejné obstarávanie (nadlimitné zákazky)
why_relevant: Slovenská pošta is a state-owned operator of a large branch cash network and is closely tied to Poštová banka's Poštomat ATM network. Its tenders cover cash transport, security, branch cash handling and payment-acceptance IT, exposing counts of branches, devices and cash volumes.

source_name: Slovenská záručná a rozvojová banka – CRZ contract listing
why_relevant: A state-owned bank whose full contract set is published in CRZ — including IT, card/payment-service and cash-handling suppliers. Provides a rare readable view of an actual bank's vendor stack and pricing.

source_name: eGovZmluvy (zmluvy.egov.sk) – municipal/school contract publishing register
source_subtype: third-party disclosure register for local government
why_relevant: Many municipalities, schools and contributory organisations publish contracts and orders here (with CRZ interlinking). Captures the long tail of small POS-terminal, cash-register and cash-collection purchases invisible in above-threshold registers.

source_name: Transparency International Slovensko – Otvorené verejné obstarávanie (tender.sme.sk)
why_relevant: NGO-built institution profiles covering contracts since 2005 (>€60k) and since April 2011 all above €10k. Useful for long historical back-series and for supplier concentration analysis in payments/cash services.

source_name: Nadácia Zastavme korupciu – procurement watchdog analyses
why_relevant: Watchdog investigations dissect specific SK tenders (e.g. a ~€4m Slovenská pošta security tender) and expose technical specifications, incumbent suppliers and vendor lock-in — narrative context and hard detail that raw registers do not surface.

source_name: FinStat.sk – supplier/company financials cross-reference
why_relevant: Links winning suppliers of payment/ATM/cash contracts to their revenues, ownership and public-contract totals, converting a list of awards into a supplier market-share view of the SK payments services market.

source_name: Obchodný vestník (Commercial Bulletin, justice.gov.sk)
why_relevant: Statutory commercial gazette carrying corporate, insolvency, auction and some procurement-adjacent notices for SK entities; useful for tracking the corporate lifecycle of payment/ATM service suppliers identified from contract awards.

source_name: Ministerstvo obrany SR – verejné obstarávanie (example ministry buyer profile)
why_relevant: Illustrates the standard per-ministry procurement page pattern in SK. Every ministry, Sociálna poisťovňa, Finančná správa and Štátna pokladnica maintains an equivalent page — collectively the enumerable set of public buyers of card-acceptance and cash services.

source_name: Finančná správa SR – published documents and procurement (eKasa / cashless acceptance mandate)
why_relevant: The tax authority publishes methodological guidance and legislative documents on eKasa and, under Act 384/2025, the obligation from 1 March 2026 for sellers to enable cashless payment above €1 — a regulatory driver of POS terminal demand. Its own procurement (eKasa infrastructure) is a further quantitative source.

source_name: Global Payments Slovensko (Erste/Slovenská sporiteľňa acquiring JV) - corporate site
why_relevant: Dominant SK card acquirer/processor (JV of Global Payments Inc., Erste Group/Slovenská sporiteľňa, formerly also CaixaBank). Public SK-language pages quantify the deployment: >37,000 terminals in Slovakia and >EUR 2bn of transactions processed annually. Terminal-model pages (Ingenico Lane 3600, Self 2000/4000, PAX IM30/A920, Nexgo UN20) reveal the actual hardware fleet mix in SK acceptance.

source_name: Slovenská sporiteľňa - POS / acquiring partner pages (bank-side vendor disclosure)
source_subtype: bank product page naming a vendor
why_relevant: Largest SK bank publicly names its acquiring supplier and the terminal offer. Bank-side confirmation of the vendor relationship is stronger evidence than the vendor claim alone, and the EN mirror (/en/business/receiving-payments/pos) lists accepted schemes and terminal types.

source_name: Printec Slovakia (ex-NCR Slovensko) - country page, Printec Group
why_relevant: Principal SK channel for NCR/NCR Atleos ATMs, payment terminals, kiosks and self-checkout, plus outsourcing/maintenance of bank self-service estates. Self-describes as one of the main SK providers of payment terminals, NCR ATMs and SCO; portfolio pages signal what SK banks are buying (Android POS platform, ATM software, P2PE, eKASA-compatible AdeoPOS).

source_name: Printec Group - ATM & POS Landscape in CEE research series
why_relevant: Vendor-published multi-country (14 CEE markets) ATM/EFT-POS estate research that normally includes Slovakia rows - a rare vendor-side quantitative series on device counts and channel trends. Gated landing pages (offer.printecgroup.com) suggest lead-capture forms.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf - banking case studies / success stories library
why_relevant: DN publishes quantified ATM-estate case studies for CEE banks (e.g. a CSOB case study citing end-to-end ATM network outsourcing and 99.8% uptime over a ~20-year relationship; bank99 six-year ATM-as-a-Service). CSOB has a Slovak arm, so the CEE case-study library is the highest-yield vendor surface for SK/CZ ATM outsourcing evidence. Note: I did not find a case study explicitly scoped to Slovakia.

source_name: NCR Atleos - banking / ATM-as-a-Service and services pages
why_relevant: World's largest ATM deployer (claims 800k+ ATMs, 140+ countries) and the OEM behind the Printec-distributed SK estate. Useful for tracking ATM-as-a-Service / managed-services model shifts that would show up in SK bank estates, and for identifying which SK institutions may move off owned hardware.

source_name: Asseco Central Europe - Referencie (SK banking references)
why_relevant: Largest SK-headquartered banking-software supplier. Public SK references and press pages name Slovenská sporiteľňa, 365.bank/Poštová banka, Societe Generale, J&T Finance Group and RBI Group, and describe long-running core banking (eStarBANK / Core Banking System) and card-transaction-processing engagements incl. Google/Apple Pay backend and internet/mobile banking backends (e.g. Poštová banka on Asseco core for ~24 years).

source_name: Forbes Slovensko - 'Banky sa svojimi IT dodávateľmi nechvália'
why_relevant: Key meta-source: SK business press piece explaining exactly why supplier-side evidence is scarce - banks white-label vendor work and sometimes contractually forbid suppliers from listing them as references. It also names vendors and their SK bank customers, so it doubles as an actor-map seed and as the rationale for the collection strategy of this cell.

source_name: SOFTEC - Projekty (SK banking project references)
why_relevant: SK integrator publishing named bank project write-ups: unified front-end / branch system for Raiffeisen, biometric remote client verification for Tatra banka, NFINITY digital onboarding for CSOB. Gives channel-strategy and branch-system detail otherwise invisible outside procurement.

source_name: Millennium.sk - Referencie (bank CRM/digital projects)
why_relevant: SK integrator with per-bank case pages: Erste Private Banking CRM, Slovenská sporiteľňa corporate CRM migration to Dynamics 365 cloud, Raiffeisenbank knowledge base. Useful for mapping which SK banks are on which vendor stacks and for cloud-adoption signals.
